note: Synthetic prompts for future independent response-behavior replay. Presence and structure tests do not prove model compliance. No private case text.

cases.purpose: Differentiate an unsent supervisor draft idea from delivered advice
cases.synthetic_input: A supervisor drafted advice to remove an online shopping app but never sent it. A client has now replied with a description of a stressful evening. The proposed advice can still be useful.
cases.failure_example: As I mentioned before, did you already remove the app?
cases.pass_criterion: Introduce the app-removal idea as a new suggestion; do not refer to it as something the client was told or imply they replied to it.

cases.purpose: Keep a selected symptom-management focus grouped after other topics
cases.synthetic_input: A client says a breathing exercise relaxes their shoulders in a few breaths; a recent shopping conflict and a sleep question are also present. The primary target is how breathing affects anxiety when sustained.
cases.failure_example: Open on breathing, switch to shopping and sleep, then repeat the breathing discussion at the end.
cases.pass_criterion: Give relevant secondary issues brief separate coverage, then one contiguous breathing block containing history, observed partial effect, and a single question about continuation and carryover.

cases.purpose: Prior quitting experience must inform coping advice before withdrawal talk
cases.synthetic_input: The record documents several periods of easy discontinuation of an unwanted coping behavior, but also repeated restarts after nights of poor sleep. The latest client asks how to avoid reaching for the same behavior again.
cases.failure_example: Launch a new withdrawal management plan without addressing the reliable overnight benefit or prior easy discontinuations.
cases.pass_criterion: Recognize that restarting is the current issue; identify the immediate need and feasible safer ways of meeting it; preserve urgency if new impairment is present.

cases.purpose: Do not turn a narrow somatic cue or calm-looking video into proof of symptom absence
cases.synthetic_input: The person reports their shoulders loosen after three breaths but does not say the anxiety goes away. A shared public video shows them smiling, which reveals nothing certain about subjective anxiety.
cases.failure_example: Your anxiety disappears within three breaths, and the video proves you are not anxious most days.
cases.pass_criterion: Distinguish tension easing from anxiety relief, avoid inferring internal state from appearance, and ask whether longer practice preserves or extends actual felt benefit.

cases.purpose: Preserve inclusive speaker terms across languages and ask direct value questions
cases.synthetic_input: A supervisor refers to retreat support from monastics, meaning both women and men, and wants to know which aspect of a client's intense sense of being alive matters most and which harmless activities already help.
cases.failure_example: Translate monastics as monks only; give a long speculative list of reasons for feeling alive and fail to ask about past safe alternatives.
cases.pass_criterion: Preserve monks and nuns or an inclusive equivalent; ask the person directly what matters most about feeling alive and which non-harmful experiences already supply some of it.
